hook: They flew straight into a 220 mph hurricane.
narration: This plane was flying into the strongest hurricane the National Hurricane Center had ever tracked.
It was Hurricane Patricia, and a NOAA Orion crew was headed for the eyewall.
NOAA's hunters measured winds of one hundred ninety-two knots up there, [short pause] over two hundred twenty miles an hour.
They fly through on purpose and drop sensors that radio back wind and pressure all the way down to the sea.
outcome: The crew flew the Orion through Patricia's eyewall and into the calm eye.
title: Flying into a 220 mph hurricane
description:
A NOAA WP-3D Orion hurricane hunter crew flies through the eyewall of Hurricane Patricia in 2015, the strongest hurricane on record in the National Hurricane Center's area.

Footage: NOAA video by Lonnie Kregelka, via Wikimedia Commons: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Hurricane_Patricia_Seen_from_NOAA_Hurricane_Hunter_Aircraft.webm

extra_sources.excerpt: This makes Patricia the strongest hurricane on record in the National Hurricane Center's area of responsibility
A NOAA Hurricane Hunter aircraft reported that Patricia changed little in intensity through about 1800 UTC. The aircraft measured 192 kt flight-level winds at 700 mb in the southeastern eyewall,

drop_reason: Opening is flat gray cloud and the cockpit shots are washed-out silhouettes; nothing on screen shows the 220 mph danger. Hurricane-hunter footage needs visible turbulence or the stadium-effect eye to work.
